grade.reason: match starter's darkness (floor L~21.7) while keeping the flooded biome's teal hue readable
grade.reference: art/tiles/starter/work/mockA2_floor_ref.png (reused starter's own reference -- 'similar darkness to starter' per the brief)
grade.history_round1_additive_rejected: starter used postprocess.py's built-in ADDITIVE grade (L_new = L_old + l_offset). Reproducing that here with l_offset=-12.85 (derived from this biome's sample) CLIPPED the darkest rock/water tiles (raw L 5.5-14) to a hard L=0 -- confirmed both numerically and visually (a lone pillar and 2x2 pillar block rendered as flat solid-black squares).
grade.history_round2_single_multiplicative_sti: fixed round 1's hard clip with a single MULTIPLICATIVE Lab transform (L_new = L_old * l_scale) instead of additive, calibrated from the same sample/ref pair (l_scale=0.6277, chroma_scale=0.6525), applied uniformly to the whole rock+water+floor-variant family. This removed the hard clip (darkest rock tile L=3.5, not 0) but the coordinator/user's review of the delivered gate artifacts still called the pillars out as reading like 'flat black squares' -- correct: L=3.5 with proportionally-compressed contrast is still perceptually near-invisible at thumbnail scale, well below starter's own accepted deep-rock benchmark (starter shipped rock mask-15 at L=6.84, c=1.94; shipped water mask-15 at L=5.75, c=3.38, post-fill). A single transform calibrated to the FLOOR sample cannot simultaneously hit the floor's target darkness AND a readable rock/water darkness when the raw upper-terrain art starts this much darker than starter's did -- the two targets pull in opposite directions (floor needs L_old*0.63, rock needs L_old*1.24 to reach a readable target); no single scalar satisfies both.
grade.round3_final_two_tier_grade: once `unifyfloor` (see below) existed, the floor and upper-terrain calibration problems could be decoupled, because unifyfloor REPLACES every floor-classified pixel of a corner tile with the exact reference-floor pixel regardless of what grade produced it beforehand -- so only the genuinely-kept 'upper' pixels need to look good on their own terms. Final pipeline per corner-set tile: (1) grade the RAW tile with `floorGrade` (the round-2 multiplicative transform, l_scale=0.6277/chroma_scale=0.6525) purely so its floor-coloured pixels land close enough to the true floor reference for unifyfloor's Lab-distance classifier to recognise and replace them correctly -- this input is discarded for any pixel unifyfloor keeps; (2) run unifyfloor against the repaired+floorGrade'd rock tile_15 to get the corrected floor pixels + an implicit keep/replace mask (diffed against step 1's input); (3) separately grade the SAME raw tile with a per-set `rockUpperGrade`/`waterUpperGrade` transform calibrated directly toward starter's own accepted deep-rock/deep-water benchmarks (not the floor's); (4) composite: floor-classified pixels from step 2 (correct, halo-free), everything else from step 3 (readable, non-crushed upper texture). Re-verified: darkest rock tile now L=6.90/c=2.01 (target was L=6.84/c=1.94), darkest water tile L=5.60/c=3.30 (target L=5.75/c=3.38) -- both match starter's own shipped darkness almost exactly, and the room mockup shows clearly textured (not flat) pillars with visible algae-streak detail.

unifyfloor.reason: user-approved fix (coordinator follow-up): every pool, and to a lesser extent every rock edge, was surrounded by a grey band a tile wide, because each corner-set tile's own independently-generated floor-region pixels never quite matched the canonical pure-floor tile's grain/tone. Added by a concurrent agent as a new `unifyfloor` subcommand in scripts/tiles/postprocess.py (already present when checked -- no wait needed): classifies each tile's pixels by Lab-colour distance to a palette built from the floor reference, and REPLACES only the classified-floor pixels with the same-position pixel from the reference, leaving upper-terrain (rock/water) pixels -- including their edge/transition pixels -- untouched.

diagnosedNotFixed.diagnosis: raw-art defect, not a pipeline bug -- reported per instructions, NOT rerolled, zero spend. The 'relic_light' floor variant (picked as tile_7 from job 23594b17-...) has a light grey vertical stripe baked into its raw generated pixels, present before any matching/grading (confirmed by inspecting art/tiles/flooded/work/floor_variants_picked/relic_light.png directly). Checked all 16 raw floor-variant tiles: EVERY candidate showing the 'tiny teal light' motif (tile_3, tile_7, tile_11, tile_15 -- the entire rightmost column of the job's internal 4x4 generation canvas) carries the same vertical-bar artifact, and several neighbouring tiles (tile_9, tile_12, tile_14) show a matching bar on a different edge. This reads as a canvas-tiling/grid-divider bleed from the generation itself, not something post-processing introduced -- there is no clean alternative among the already-generated candidates to substitute in its place. The two occurrences in the mockup are simply this one defective source tile being placed twice by the deterministic per-room floor-variant hash. A reroll of the floor-variant job (with the light motif isolated to its own single-item job, away from the canvas edge) would likely fix it, but that requires new PixelLab spend, which this follow-up explicitly ruled out -- reporting only, per instructions.
